author: 1337isnot1337, with substantial AI assistance from Kimi
statement: The unweighted highest-charge scalarity and length rules are valid, but the registered uniform central-interval construction is false as stated. A complete h=3 tensor computation shows that roots of the scalar filter polynomial do not kill its charge-projected pieces, so omitting |s|<2 leaves a nonzero non-scalar crossing defect. Multiplying the projected pieces by an additional rooted polynomial also fails. Two normalization errors are identified and repaired for the full unfiltered identity. The former conditional rho(epsilon) and alpha claims are withdrawn; no uniform filter or improved bound is claimed.
remaining_obligations: A uniform central filter must control the complete omitted tensor sum or use a different recovery mechanism
Any successor must prove leading capacity, both directional ranks, uniform entry heights and full transfer costs
The counterexample does not refute the separate finite raw-charge witnesses or every possible charge filter
Independent review of the counterexample and predecessor arguments
